(vii) Subject to existing laws, establish and provide for the maintenance, repair and operation of an efficient waterworks system to supply water r the inhabitants and to purify the source of the water uppl • xxx" We responded to said query by way Of DIL Opinion No. 18 s. 2018 stating that local governments are bereft of authori to ant water and sanitation franchise. This opinion was based on interplo atio that P.D. 1076, otherwise known as the "Water Code of the Philippines" (Water e), falls squarely within the phrase "subject to existing laws" which premised the abovecited Section 458(a)(5)(vii) of the LGC. And that, under this Water Code and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), it is the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) that has the power to grant water permits. It bears noting that the query used the term "franchise" to mean a license/permit to operate a water and sanitation business or activity within the territorial jurisdiction of the LGU concerned which necessarily includes extraction or utilization of subterranean or ground water and its distribution. Otherwise, the query could have specified the extent of what it referred by " er and sanitation franchise". At any rate, in the case of Metropolitan ebu aterDistrict(MCWD) vs. Margarita A. Adalal, it was mentioned that the Suprem Court, in Philippine Airlines, Inc. v. Civil Aeronautics Board, "has t m franchise broadly so as to include, not only authorizations issuing directly from Congress in the form of statute, but also thosegranted by administrativeagehcies which thepower togrant franchises has been delegated by Congress, to wit: Congress has granted certain administrative agencies the power to grant licenses for, or to authorize the operation ofcertain public utilities. With the growing complexity of modern life, the multiplication of the subjects of governmental regulation, and the increased difficulty of administering the laws, there is a constantly growing tendency towards the delegation of greater powers by the legislature, and towards the approval of the practice by the courts. It is generally recognized that a franchise may be derived indirectly from the state through a duly designated agency, and to this extent, the power to grant franchises has frequently been delegated, even to In pursuance of this, it has been agencies other than those Ofa legislative na held that privileges conferred by grant by I I authorities as agents Tor the state constitute as much a legislative franchis as ugh the grant had been made by an act of the Legislature. Relevant to herein subject matter is a news article published by The Daily Guardian in its website http://thedailyguardian.net which discussed about the assailed DILG Opinion No. 18 s. 2018. (A copy of this Article is attached hereto for a ready reference.) Reportedly, the city government of Iloilo entered into a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with South Balibago Reso ces, Inc. (SBRI) to serve the demands of concessionaires which were not met Me o Iloilo Water District (MIWD), the city's sole water distributor. ent , MIWD sued the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SIC) for granting the franchise SBRI. This action on the part of the concern LGU may be viewed in relation to Section 46 of P.D. No. 198, as amendeå, which "ovid "Section 46. Exclusive Franchise. - No franchise shall be granted to any other person or agency for domestic water service within the district or any portion thereof unless and except to the extent that the board of directors of said district consents thereto by resolution duly adopted." Hence, it is understood that the Local Waters Utilities Administration (LWUA) shall not grant a franchise to any other applicant if a water district is already existing and the consent of its Board of Directors was not secured. This rule stands regardless of whether the concerned local legislative body d passed a resolution forming a new water district because pursuant to Sec. f P. . No. 198, "Once formed, a district is

subject to the provisions of this Act and under the jurisdiction of any political subdivision. " 7. Had it been mentioned, the Department should have evaded rendering an opinion based on the Sub Judice Rule. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
